text:
Why does a computer need examples in order to learn to recognize earthquakes?

A computer can’t simply "find earthquakes." Humans need to decide what data to provide, identify examples, determine what patterns matter. Let’s look at seismic data from Anchorage. Can you find earthquakes?

Instructions

1) In the "WaveRunner 1" tile under Challenge 2, Click on the box that says “Choose a station” scroll through the list and choose one seismograph station around Anchorage.

2) Click on the box that says “Choose a model” and click on “compact model.”

3) Type in a date range (anytime between January 1, 2018 to the present day).

4) Click the "Timeline It!" button (the button furthest to the right) in the bottom control bar of the WaveRunner tile. The Timeline tile will display the data for the station and dates you selected right below this WaveRunner tile.

5) Use the Timeline tile to search through the seismic data for signals of earthquakes. Be sure to check that each signal you choose matches the shape of the ones above!

6) When you have found a signal, record its characteristics in the table.
